[MUQATIL:16:3-5/r2] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The human created from a sperm drop is Ubayy b. Khalaf al-Jumahi, whom the Prophet killed at Uhud.
[MUQATIL:16:3-5/r3] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Ubayy challenged the Prophet about how God could resurrect bones, crushing and scattering them in the wind; the same challenge appears in 36:78. | mentions 36:78

[ZAJJAJ:v3p190/r5] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | This verse abbreviates the account of human development; the Qur'an recounts the changing stages of human life elsewhere.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r1] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | خصيم means someone who argues in a dispute.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r2] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | مبين describes someone who clearly expresses what is within him.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r3] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | The contrast displays God's power in bringing a human from a lowly drop to eloquence and capability.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r4] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | The description should make people recognize God's favor in bringing them from a lowly drop to their present state.

[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r6] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · الكلبي | reports | Al-Kalbi says the verse was revealed about Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who scattered decayed bones and challenged the possibility of resurrection.
[WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p278#2/r1] WAHIDI-ASBAB, d. 468 · author | reports | The verse was revealed when Ubayy ibn Khalaf brought the Prophet a decayed bone and challenged whether God could revive it.
[WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p278#2/r2] WAHIDI-ASBAB, d. 468 · author | holds | The author links this verse to the parallel passage in Yasin, which he says was revealed about the same incident. | mentions 36:77
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#4/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · أبو إسحاق | reports | Abu Ishaq says this verse compresses the account of human development, which the Qur’an describes in detail elsewhere.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas glosses the words as “I created.”
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · المفسرون | reports | The commentators say this verse and 36:77 were revealed concerning Ubayy ibn Khalaf and his denial of resurrection. | mentions 36:77
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · أهل اللغة | reports | Khaṣīm means disputant, as in 4:105; the lexicographers analyze faʿīl as carrying the sense of an active participant and cite nasīb, ʿashīr, akīl, and sharīb. | mentions 4:105
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · أهل اللغة | reports | Alternatively, khaṣīm may be an active form from khaṣama/yakhṣimu, meaning “to dispute”; Hamza’s reading yakhṣimūn at 36:49 illustrates this formation. | mentions 36:49
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | Mubīn means apparent, so the person is clearly contentious; it can also mean that he articulates his contention, though falsely.

[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:1-4/r9] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | The human created from a drop of fluid is Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p9/r2] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Humans are created from a drop yet become manifest disputants, arguing falsely.

[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p378#2/r11] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · قيل | reports | A report says this verse was revealed in response to Ubayy ibn Khalaf’s challenge, ‘Who revives the bones when they are dust?’ | mentions 36:78

[RAZI-FULL:v19p178#3/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | After using the celestial bodies as evidence for a wise creator, Rāzī turns to the human, the noblest body after the heavens: its creation from sperm points through the body, and its disputatious intellect through the soul.
[RAZI-FULL:v19p178#3/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الأطباء | reports | Some physicians say sperm is internally heterogeneous: food undergoes four digestions in the stomach, liver, veins, and organs, whose substances form tissues; bodily heat during desire then liquefies material from the organs into sperm.
[RAZI-FULL:v19p178#3/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | If sperm is homogeneous, its inherent natural force acting by necessity on homogeneous matter should produce a sphere; since animal bodies are not spherical, their formation requires a wise, deliberate creator.

[RAZI-FULL:v19p179/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Natural forces would make each simple constituent spherical, yielding an animal of joined spheres; celestial influences are also inadequate because they are uniform, so the bodies are governed by a wise, voluntary agent.
[RAZI-FULL:v19p179/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | A newborn human is less perceptive than a chick, which already distinguishes danger, allies, and suitable food; later the human mind reaches extraordinary knowledge and disputation, a transition from deficiency to perfection requiring wise divine governance.
